title: Mass on a spring
summary: Underdamped: oscillates with period 698.7 ms while the swing halves every 158.4 ms.

methods.name: Exact solution
methods.reason: A linear equation with constant coefficients has a closed-form solution.

steps.title: Set up the equation from Newton's second law
steps.text: Mass times acceleration equals the sum of the forces. \(k x\) is the spring force (Hooke's law), pulling back towards the unstretched length. \(c\,dx/dt\) is the damping force, proportional to speed and opposing the motion.

steps.title: List the known values
steps.text: Everything is converted to SI units before it goes into the equation.

steps.title: Solve the differential equation
steps.text: This is a linear second-order equation with constant coefficients. The damping ratio \(\zeta = 0.438\) is below 1 (underdamped): it oscillates while the swing dies away.
latex: x_h(t) = e^{-\gamma t}\left(A\cos\omega_d t + B\sin\omega_d t\right)

substeps.title: Characteristic equation
substeps.text: Try \(x = e^{rt}\) in the equation with the right-hand side set to zero.

substeps.title: Apply the initial conditions
substeps.text: Set \(x(0) = x_0\) and \(x'(0) = v_0\) and solve the two equations for \(A\) and \(B\).

steps.title: Energy check
steps.text: The energy stored in the spring and the motion falls as the damper turns it into heat. Over the time shown, the energy lost equals the work done against damping, \(\int c\,v^2\,dt\).

steps.title: Compare with the ideal case
steps.text: With no damping, driving or gravity it would swing for ever with amplitude 5 cm (0.05 m) and period 628.3 ms.

steps.title: Answer
steps.text: Underdamped: oscillates with period 698.7 ms while the swing halves every 158.4 ms.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked against a direct step-by-step integration of the equation, and the initial displacement and velocity are reproduced.

methods.verify_note: Checked against a direct step-by-step integration of the equation, and the initial displacement and velocity are reproduced.
